test_command: dotnet build api/Biolog.Api/Biolog.Api.csproj && dotnet test tests/features/bio-int-002/Biolog.Features.Integrations.Tests.csproj && dotnet test tests/dotnet/Biolog.IntegrationTests/Biolog.IntegrationTests.csproj && bash tests/features/bio-int-002/BIO-INT-002.test.sh
notes:
Round 7: remediates BIO-INT-002-F07 (Zainab round-6 FAIL, evidence/features/bio-int-002/codex/SECURITY-REVIEW-ZAINAB-ROUND6.md, confirmed by Seyi after an initial provisional pass was reversed and then corrected again) against commit 8ab0c83/ffa6a10.

Finding: ComputeFingerprint joined external keys, field names and field values with raw, unescaped ';:,=' delimiters - not injective. A field map {"a": "b,c=d"} and {"a": "b", "c": "d"} both produced the literal segment 'a=b,c=d' and hashed identically. After a claim release (round 6's own fix), a request carrying one of these colliding-but-different payloads could pass round 6's own fingerprint-match check and still land in the replay branch with stale, disagreeing provenance - defeating round 6's exact protection.

Seyi's own round-7 review initially read this as triggering the architecture-checkpoint round cap (a third-in-a-row downstream recovery gap) and reversed an earlier provisional pass to say so explicitly. God's recorded decision after both reviewers weighed in: this does NOT trigger the cap. The cap is about the create/orphan/provenance/link/audit SEQUENCING and atomicity design recurring as the source of each new gap (rounds 2 through 6); F07 is a narrow, well-understood, mechanical bug one layer below that - a non-injective serialization in one helper function, with an unambiguous correct answer, unrelated to what gets retained, released, or ordered across the recovery chain's stores. Proceeded as a normal fix, no Kemi, no architecture escalation.

Fixed: ComputeFingerprint now hashes a canonical JSON serialization (mappingId plus rows sorted by external key, each row's fields sorted by key) instead of hand-rolled delimiter concatenation. JSON's own string quoting/escaping rules make the serialized form unambiguous regardless of what characters appear in an external key, field name, or field value - two distinct (mappingId, rows) inputs can no longer produce the same canonical text. ComputeFingerprint was widened from private to internal (same test-visibility convention ReconcileStrandedCardsAsync uses in BIO-VIS-002) so tests can assert on its output directly.

Four new tests: (1)/(2) two direct ComputeFingerprint collision tests reproducing both distinct ambiguities the old scheme had (a field value embedding the field-separator syntax, and a field value embedding the row-separator syntax), each proving the two former-collision inputs now hash differently. (3) an end-to-end regression: after a claim release, a retry using one of these formerly-colliding-but-now-distinguished payloads is correctly routed through fresh classification (F06's own replay-mismatch path) and surfaces a Conflict rather than a silent Created, never mints a second PERSON. (4) implicitly covered: the existing round-6 same-content/different-content regression tests still pass unchanged, confirming no behavior regression for already-tested cases.

Verified: dotnet build clean (sandbox restore-socket flake on first dotnet test attempt - System.Net.Sockets.SocketException (13) Permission denied on the VSTest loopback socket - resolved with sandbox disabled). BIO-INT-002 unit tests 43/43 (was 40/40). BIO-INT-002 structural harness 76/76 (was 72/72). Full Biolog.IntegrationTests: 192/192, no regression. Scope confirmed clean via git status - only api/features/bio-int-002/ImportBatchService.cs, docs/features/bio-int-002/README.md, tests/features/bio-int-002/BIO-INT-002.test.sh, tests/features/bio-int-002/ImportBatchServiceTests.cs touched.

Round 6: remediates BIO-INT-002-F06 (Seyi round-6 FAIL, evidence/BIO-INT-002/codex/REVIEW-Seyi-round6.md) against commit e8ba907/2b44b37. Zainab PASSED round 5 outright - only this one finding needed closing, and it was explicitly flagged as the architecture-checkpoint finding (the third consecutive round where closing one failure-recovery point in the create-orphan-provenance-link-audit chain opened another just downstream of it).

Finding: IIdempotencyStore.Release deletes the claim record AND its own stored RequestFingerprint entirely, but IImportRowProvenanceLedger's recorded row outcomes carried no fingerprint of their own and were never cleaned up. So a released attempt's AC05 content-reuse protection vanished along with the claim, while the attempt's own recovery state (orphan ledger, provenance ledger) survived untouched. A later request reusing the same (tenant, idempotency key, mapping, external key) with genuinely DIFFERENT row content could win a fresh claim (no live record left to compare a fingerprint against) and land straight in the replay branch, which trusted stale provenance without ever re-evaluating content - silently linking the new request to the ORIGINAL attempt's PERSON and reporting a clean Created, reintroducing AC04's exact silent-overwrite problem through a path none of rounds 2-5 had touched.

This was escalated directly to god rather than patched a fourth time, per the checkpoint. God's recorded decision: extend the existing durable-ledger pattern with one more field, not a cross-store transactional rewrite (this codebase has no shared transactional substrate across the claim store, orphan ledger, provenance ledger, link store and audit sink - building one would be Kemi-scale, the same proportionality standard already applied to BIO-VIS-002's own outbox-pattern question). A follow-up, more specific course-correction then replaced an initially-drafted separate new ledger (IReleasedAttemptFingerprintLedger) with the simpler mechanism actually shipped: carry the fingerprint as one more field on the EXISTING IImportRowProvenanceLedger entry, rather than introduce a second ledger.

Fixed: IImportRowProvenanceLedger.RecordAsync now also takes the recording attempt's own whole-batch ComputeFingerprint value (already computed once per ApplyAsync call - no new per-row hash), and FindAsync returns both the outcome and the fingerprint it was recorded under (a new small ImportRowProvenanceEntry record). The replay branch in ApplyAsync's row loop now compares the stored fingerprint against the CURRENT request's own fingerprint before trusting a replay: a match proceeds exactly as every prior round's own resume-after-failure tests already prove; a mismatch falls through to fresh classification instead of a silent adopt - which, since the orphan ledger entry is still genuinely unresolved (no link exists for that external key yet), lands in round 2's own content-aware adoption check and correctly surfaces a Conflict rather than a clean Created. No new ledger, no change to the shared IIdempotencyStore contract, no Kemi.

Two new tests: (1) a released claim reused with DIFFERENT content for the same external key - asserts the outcome is Conflict (never a silent Created), correctly identifies the disagreeing PersonId, never links under the disagreeing content, and never mints a second PERSON. (2) a released claim reused with the SAME content - the positive counterpart, proving the fingerprint comparison never rejects a legitimate same-content retry.

Round cap restated: if a future review finds yet another distinct gap in this same create/orphan/provenance/link/audit recovery chain, the next action is to stop and escalate directly rather than attempt another local patch - at that point it would mean the recovery model itself needs a from-scratch redesign with Kemi, not another incremental fix.

Verified: dotnet build clean. BIO-INT-002 unit tests 40/40 (was 38/38). BIO-INT-002 structural harness 72/72 (was 67/67). Full Biolog.IntegrationTests: 192/192, no regression.

Round 5: remediates ZAINAB-INT-002-F05 (Zainab round-4 FAIL, evidence/features/bio-int-002/codex/SECURITY-REVIEW-ZAINAB-ROUND4.md) against commit 90e4055. Seyi PASSED round 4 outright - only this one finding needed closing.

Finding: RecordRowProvenanceSafelyAsync ran AFTER linkStore.CreateAsync had already durably created the link. A genuine provenance-write failure released the idempotency claim with a real link but no provenance record - a retry's ClassifyRowAsync then found that link and returned Unchanged, never re-entering the Created branch, losing the original Created provenance entirely.

Fixed by reordering, not new machinery: provenance is now recorded BEFORE the link is created, for every row, right when its outcome reaches final form. The replay branch (a provenance record already exists for this idempotency attempt) now also idempotently ensures the link exists before continuing.

Verified: BIO-INT-002 unit tests 38/38. BIO-INT-002 structural harness 67/67. Full Biolog.IntegrationTests: 192/192, no regression.

Finding 1 (Seyi F04 = Zainab round-3 finding 1): round-2's own fix moved the authoritative Active/SyncDirection re-read and guard checks to AFTER the per-mapping lock but still BEFORE the release-on-failure try/catch - stranding the idempotency key InFlight forever on a disabled mapping, direction flip, vanished mapping, or cancellation post-claim. Fixed: lock acquisition, the fresh mapping read, and both guard checks now ALL live inside the same try/catch as the rows loop and batch/audit/persist.

Finding 2 (Zainab round-3 finding 2, ZAINAB-INT-002-F04): IImportRowProvenanceLedger was keyed only by (TenantId, IdempotencyKey, ExternalKey) - missing MappingId, allowing cross-mapping key-reuse replay; and duplicate external keys within one request let row two replay row one's outcome. Fixed by adding MappingId to the ledger's key and rejecting duplicate external keys within a request up front.

Residual durability note (Zainab): RecordRowProvenanceBestEffortAsync's silent-swallow-any-failure stance contradicted treating Created provenance as a guaranteed remediation. Replaced with RecordRowProvenanceSafelyAsync - re-throws (failing the whole attempt, releasing the claim) if verification confirms the write genuinely never landed.

Verified: BIO-INT-002 unit tests 38/38 (was 32/32). BIO-INT-002 structural harness 67/67 (was 58/58). Full Biolog.IntegrationTests: 192/192, no regression.
